recipes.name: Vegetable Beef Soup (Fall apart beef!)
ingredients: 500g/1 lb stewing beef (, cut into 1.75cm / 2/3" cubes (Note 1))
3 carrots (, cut into 0.5 cm / 1/5" thick slices (halve larger ones))
1 1/2 cups dry red wine, Guinness beer or stout ((Note 2))
instructions: Season beef - Pat beef cubes dry with paper towels, then sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Brown beef - Heat 1 tbsp oil until very hot in a large, heavy based pot over high heat. Brown beef aggressively in 2 or 3 batches, adding more oil if needed. Remove into a bowl.
Sauté - If the pot looks dry, add a touch more oil. Add garlic and onion, cook for 2 minutes. Add carrot and celery, cook for 2 minutes or until onion is translucent.
Flour - Stir in flour, then slowly pour in beef broth while constantly stirring.
Soup broth - Add beer, water, tomato paste, bay leaves and thyme, stir well. Then add the beef back in.
Simmer 1 hour 15 minutes - Cover with lid. Adjust heat to medium low so it's bubbling gently. Simmer 1 hr 15 min or until beef is pretty tender.
Simmer 20 minutes lid off - Add potatoes and peas, simmer for a further 20 minutes without the lid. Add cooked mushrooms in the last 5 minutes.
Finish - The soup is ready when the potatoes are cooked and beef is very tender (see video). Adjust salt and pepper to taste (I like lots of pepper in this!).
Serve - Ladle into bowls. Sprinkle with parsley and serve with crusty bread if desired. Try quick Cheesy Garlic Bread or super easy Irish Soda Bread!
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium high heat. Add mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes until browned. Sprinkle with salt and pepper.

page_recipe_notes: Recipe Notes: 1. Beef – Use any stewing or braising beef, usually sold pre cut into small pieces ideal for this recipe. Otherwise, get a slow cooking cut like chuck or boneless short rib, then cut the beef into pieces. Look for beef that’s nicely marbled with fat for best results! 2. Red Wine, Guinness or Stout – will add incredible extra flavour into this soup broth! I use all 3, and enjoy them all. If you love Irish Beef Guinness Stew , you’ll know what the Guinness does to add flavour. Red wine – any dry, full bodied red wine. Cab Sauv and Merlots are ideal. Guinness Beer and Stout are dark beers, labelled as such on the cans. You should find these at most liquor stores. Use some, drink some – or tip the whole can in an simmer for longer with the lid off! Non alcoholic sub – add 400g/14 oz can of crushed tomato, 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce. This will add alternative flavour to compensate. 3. Storage – Like stew, it’s even better the next day! Will keep for 4 to 5 days in the fridge. Also freezes perfectly. 4. Nutrition per serving.
